name: SCEP
description: A SCEP (Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol) server, built on the micromdm/scep reference implementation. Apple MDM enrollment relies on a SCEP CA to issue the per-device identity certificate a device presents to the MDM server on every check-in, so this pairs with an MDM server such as NanoHUB (its -ca flag needs the CA certificate this generates). Install creates a new CA, encrypted with a random password, and enforces a random SCEP challenge password on enrollment requests.

default_credentials.password: CA key password and SCEP challenge password are generated during installation, see /opt/scep_data/scep.env

notes.text: The generated CA is self-signed and its private key (/opt/scep_data/depot/ca.key) is only as safe as this container - back it up and restrict access to it, since it can issue a trusted certificate for anyone who requests one with the challenge password.

Feed /opt/scep_data/depot/ca.pem to your MDM server's CA trust store (e.g. NanoHUB's -ca / NANOHUB_CA) and put the SCEP_CHALLENGE_PASSWORD from /opt/scep_data/scep.env into the enrollment profile's SCEP payload Challenge field.
No linux-arm64 binary is published upstream (only linux-amd64 and 32-bit linux-arm), so this only installs on amd64.
